description: AD* (Anytime Dynamic A*) plans when time is short and the world changes. Like D* Lite, it searches backwards from the goal, so its work stays valid while the start moves and edge costs change. Like ARA*, it multiplies the heuristic by a weight `w ≥ 1`, and with a *consistent* heuristic (one that never drops by more than an edge's cost along that edge) each `compute` returns a path that costs at most `w` times the optimum. A lower `w` on the next call improves the path, and `w = 1` gives an optimal one. Use it for a robot that must move now and refine its plan while it senses new obstacles.

papers.authors: Maxim Likhachev, Dave Ferguson, Geoff Gordon, Anthony Stentz, Sebastian Thrun
papers.title: Anytime Dynamic A*: An Anytime, Replanning Algorithm
papers.venue: Proceedings of the Fifteenth International Conference on Automated Planning and Scheduling (ICAPS 2005)

lineage.source: Anytime Dynamic A*: An Anytime, Replanning Algorithm: "Given the strong similarities between D* Lite and ARA*, it seems appropriate to look at whether the two could be combined into a single anytime, incremental replanning algorithm"
